name: Shimmer
description: Long reverb with a pitch shifter in its feedback loop: every pass climbs an interval, so the tail rises into a soft choir-like halo.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the reverb. Fully up is the reverb alone.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the tail rings. Bright sounds still fade sooner as Shimmer goes up, because they climb out of range.

params.name: Shimmer
params.description: How much of the tail goes through the pitch shifter on each pass. Zero is a plain reverb; higher lets more of it climb.

params.name: Interval
params.description: The step the tail moves by on every pass. The upward ones climb until they fade out of the top; Octave down sinks lower each time.

params.name: Size
params.description: How big the space sounds. Small packs the echoes close together; large spreads them out. Moving it bends the pitch of the tail.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Darkens the tail. Lower settings make the highs die away sooner and stop the shimmer from climbing as high.

params.name: Modulation
params.description: Slow drift of the delay times, which gives the tail a gentle chorus-like movement. At zero the tail is static.

params.name: Pre-delay
params.description: The gap before the reverb starts, which keeps the start of the sound clear of its tail.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Removes lows from the reverb so it does not cloud the bass. The dry signal is not touched.

params.name: Width
params.description: Stereo width of the reverb only. Zero is a mono tail; full is the widest.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The shimmer effect as Brian Eno and Daniel Lanois used it (a pitch shifter recirculating through a long reverb), built as an eight-line feedback delay network with a four-head delay-line shifter in the feedback path; not a model of any unit.
